symptoms: You will see a black velvety coating on the surface of the leaves.
In bad cases the entire tree looks black including the twigs and leaves.
The fungus grows on the sticky sugary liquid left behind by insects.
This black layer blocks the leaf from getting sunlight which hurts the plant.
favourable_conditions: High humidity and moist weather help the disease grow.
prevention: Keep your orchard clean and healthy.
Prune affected branches and destroy them right away to stop the spread.
Control insects like hoppers, aphids, and scale insects that leave sugary liquid on the plant.
practices: Manage the insects and the mould at the same time.
Prune away the parts of the tree that are covered in mould.
Burn the pruned branches to stop the disease from spreading.
Spray a starch solution on the leaves to help peel off the fungus.
